**Joe Biden's running mate and first female Vice President**
Harris was selected by Joe Biden as his running mate in 2020 and became the 49th Vice President of the United States in 2021. She was the first woman, the first African-American, and the first South Asian-American to hold the office, and this is the most common giveaway for her.

**US Senator from California**
Harris represented California in the US Senate from 2017 until becoming Vice President. She had earlier served as California's attorney general, which makes "California senator" a frequent identifying clue.

**Loretta Sanchez**
The Democratic US Representative whom Harris defeated in the 2016 Senate race, her first election for federal office. Under California's top-two primary system, the general election featured two Democrats, and Harris won with about 61 percent of the vote.

**First South Asian-American and second African-American woman in the Senate**
Harris's 2016 victory made her the first South Asian-American senator and the second Black woman to serve in the Senate, after Carol Moseley Braun of Illinois. Her mother was an Indian immigrant and her father was from Jamaica.

**"I do not believe you are a racist"**
A line Harris said to Joe Biden during a June 2019 Democratic primary debate. She went on to criticize his past opposition to federally mandated busing and his remarks about working with segregationist senators, in one of the most memorable moments of the 2020 primary.

**Busing to an integrated school**
In the same debate attack on Biden, Harris described being a little girl in California who was bused to a recently integrated school. Her campaign later sold shirts featuring a childhood photo with the line "That little girl was me."

**Record as district attorney and California attorney general**
During her 2020 presidential primary run, Harris was attacked from the left over her prosecutorial record as San Francisco District Attorney and as attorney general of California, with critics labeling her a "cop" who was too harsh on low-level offenders.

**Isaac Espinoza**
A San Francisco police officer murdered in 2004. As San Francisco District Attorney, Harris refused to seek the death penalty against his killer, which drew public criticism from Senator Dianne Feinstein at the officer's funeral.

**Abolishing private health insurance**
During a 2019 primary debate, Harris raised her hand when candidates were asked if they would abolish private health insurance in favor of a government plan. She later said she had understood the question to be about whether she would give up her own personal insurance.

**William Barr and the Mueller Report**
During a 2019 Senate Judiciary Committee hearing, Harris pressed Attorney General William Barr on whether he had personally reviewed the underlying evidence of Special Counsel Robert Mueller's report before clearing Trump of obstruction, and Barr admitted he had not.

**Jeff Sessions: "makes me nervous"**
Attorney General Jeff Sessions said Harris's rapid-fire questioning during a 2017 Senate Intelligence Committee hearing on Russian interference "makes me nervous," because she would not let him finish his answers.

**John Eastman's Newsweek op-ed**
In 2020, conservative lawyer John Eastman wrote a Newsweek op-ed questioning whether Harris was eligible to be Vice President because her parents were not US citizens when she was born in Oakland. The claim was widely condemned as a birther-style attack, and Newsweek later apologized for publishing it.

**Superheroes Are Everywhere**
A children's picture book written by Harris. In 2021 the New York Post falsely reported that copies of it were being handed out in welcome kits to migrant children at a shelter; the paper retracted the story and the reporter resigned.

**2024 presidential election**
Harris was seen as the leading Democratic figure after Joe Biden heading into 2024. After Biden withdrew in July 2024, she became the Democratic presidential nominee and lost the general election to Donald Trump.
